The 130367 is a replacement cadmium sulfide cell assembly from Resideo (Honeywell Home), 400–1000 ohm sensitivity.

The cad cell is the eye of an oil burner. It looks at the flame and its resistance drops when it sees light; the primary control reads that resistance and decides whether there is a fire. A cell that has hazed over, sooted or aged reads high, the primary decides there is no flame, and the burner locks out on a system that is actually lighting perfectly.

That is why the cell is the first thing to change on nuisance lockouts. It is the cheapest part in the sequence and the one that drifts.

Goes with: C554A1463, C554A1794.

The 32003796-001 is a thermostat cover plate from Resideo (Honeywell Home), 7-7/8 x 5-1/2 in.

Cover plates exist because the old thermostat was bigger. Replacing a wide mercury stat with a modern one leaves the paint line, the anchor holes and sometimes the whole opening on show, and the plate covers all of it in one piece.

Match the plate to the new thermostat, not to the old hole. Plates are cut for a specific series; one that does not register with the stat’s base leaves a gap on one side.

Worth measuring before ordering rather than after. The dimension that matters is the painted or papered outline the old stat left, not the thermostat that made it — twenty years of sun around a cover is a bigger rectangle than the cover was.

The alternative is patching and painting a wall to match a color that has aged. On a rental turnover or a multi-unit retrofit the plate is the cheaper answer by a wide margin, and it is done in the same visit.

The AP5208-30 is an air pressure switch from Resideo (Honeywell Home), style E121, 1/4 in barbed connection.

A pressure switch proves airflow by measuring it rather than by being pushed. It senses the pressure difference a running fan creates and makes contact when that difference appears — which works in ducts where a sail would foul, and at differentials far too small to move a vane.

Switching differential runs from about 0.02 in w.c. at the minimum set point to roughly 0.80 in w.c. at the maximum, so it covers everything from proving a small exhaust fan to confirming a blower under load.

Gold flash contacts carry pilot duty down to 10 milliamps, which matters when the load is a control input rather than a coil.

The AT120B1028 is a control transformer from Resideo (Honeywell Home), 120 Vac primary, 24 Vac secondary, foot mounted.

Almost every heating and cooling control runs on 24 volts, and the transformer is what makes it. It takes line voltage in and delivers the low-voltage supply the thermostat, the zone valves, the relays and the gas valve all share.

Size it by VA, not by voltage. Every device on the control circuit adds load — a zone valve pulls current while it drives, a relay coil holds current the whole time it is energized, a Wi-Fi thermostat draws continuously. A transformer adequate for the original equipment is not automatically adequate after two zones and a smart stat have been added, and the symptom is intermittent.

Filed here under thermostat accessories, but this is a transformer and belongs with them.

The C554A1463 is a cadmium sulfide flame detector from Resideo (Honeywell Home), type R bracket.

The cad cell is the eye of an oil burner. Its resistance falls when it sees flame, and the primary control reads that to know whether the fire lit. No flame signal inside the safety timing and the primary shuts the oil off.

Mounting matters as much as the cell. It has to see the flame and only the flame — aimed at the fire, not at the ignition arc and not at daylight through the inspection port, either of which makes the control believe in a fire that is not there.

The L4029E1029 is a high limit control from Resideo (Honeywell Home), fixed 200 °F, 3 in insert, manual reset.

The limit is the control that is supposed to never operate. It watches the plenum and breaks the burner circuit if temperature climbs past the setting — the case where the blower has failed, a filter has collapsed or a damper is shut and the heat has nowhere to go.

Manual reset is deliberate. A limit that resets itself lets the furnace keep cycling on an overheat condition and hides the fault. One that stays open forces somebody to find out why it tripped.

Insert length has to match the plenum. Too short and the element sits in the sheet metal instead of the airstream; too long and it can reach the heat exchanger.

The L4064B2228 is a fan and limit controller from Resideo (Honeywell Home), 5 in insert.

One control, two jobs, and they are not the same job. The fan side starts the blower once the plenum is warm and stops it once the heat has been delivered, so the house gets warm air instead of cold air followed by wasted heat. The limit side is the safety: it breaks the burner circuit if the plenum overheats, which is what happens when the blower fails or the return is blocked.

Insert length has to match the plenum. This is the dimension that decides whether the part fits at all, and the one most often got wrong when ordering by model number alone. Measure what comes out.

Setting the fan-on point too high is the classic complaint of cold air at the start of a cycle; setting the fan-off too high leaves usable heat in the exchanger at the end of it.

The THP2400A1019 is a thermostat cover plate from Resideo (Honeywell Home).

The VCZMA6100 is a three-way VC cartridge cage valve from Resideo (Honeywell Home), 1/2 in sweat, 3.7 Cv, linear flow.

Three-way means the water always has somewhere to go. When the zone is satisfied the valve diverts flow to the bypass instead of stopping it, so the circulator never ends up pushing against a closed system — the case that makes pumps noisy and short-lived.

Linear flow is the reason to pick this over a quick-opening valve. Flow follows stem position proportionally, so a control that modulates gets an usable response across the whole travel rather than most of the flow appearing in the first fraction of the stroke.

The cartridge cage design puts the working parts in a replaceable cartridge inside the bronze body. The body stays soldered or threaded into the pipe; what wears comes out.

With a VC series actuator the on/off models drive in about 6 seconds. Close-off is 60 psi, well above what a residential loop develops.

The actuator is sold separately. This is the valve assembly; pair it with a VC series actuator.

A supply line that weeps behind a wall, a water heater that lets go while the house is empty, a washing machine hose at the end of its life — all of it runs until somebody notices, and the cost is the drying and the rebuild rather than the water.

This is the part that ends it. The actuator drives a full-port ball valve on the main; when the sensor finds water, or when you close it from the app, the supply stops. A detector tells you there is a leak. A valve stops it while you are in another state.

Size it to the main, not to the fixture — this one is 1/2 in NPT. The valve is lead-free because it sits in potable supply.

In the box: L5 actuator, lead-free ball valve, power supply adapter, actuator to ball valve metal clip, 5 ft water leak detector cable.

Mount orientation is free, which matters where the main enters at an awkward angle.

The WLD3CABLE is a cable sensor for the L1 Wi-Fi water leak and freeze detector from Resideo (Honeywell Home).

A detector only senses where it sits. The cable sensor turns a point into a line: run it along the base of a water heater, behind a washing machine or under a sink, and any part of that run finding water is a detection.

Cables chain together, so the sensing area extends as far as the layout needs.

The YTH6320R1001 is a programmable thermostat from Resideo (Honeywell Home), supplied as a kit.

A programmable thermostat pays for itself on the hours nobody is home. Setting back eight degrees for the working day and again overnight is the single largest saving available on an existing system, and it only happens reliably when the schedule does it instead of a person.

The failure mode of a programmable stat is being left on permanent hold. If the schedule is going to be overridden within a week, a non-programmable stat does the same job with fewer buttons — and that is an honest recommendation, not a smaller sale.

This version ships as a kit with the sensor and equipment module, so the wireless system is commissioned as a matched set.

The YTHX9421R5101WW is a Prestige thermostat from Resideo (Honeywell Home), supplied as a kit, Up to 4 Heat/2 Cool Heat Pumps; Up to 3 Heat/2 Cool Conventional Systems.

A thermostat earns its price on the equipment it can drive properly, not on the screen. Multi-stage heating, a heat pump with auxiliary, humidification and ventilation are all decisions the thermostat makes or fails to make; a stat that can only switch one stage runs two-stage equipment as though it were single-stage and throws away the efficiency that was paid for.

This one drives Up to 4 Heat/2 Cool Heat Pumps; Up to 3 Heat/2 Cool Conventional Systems. Check that against the equipment before ordering — it is the specification that decides whether the install works, and the one most often skipped in favor of the feature list.

RedLINK is what lets it work with wireless sensors, outdoor sensors and equipment modules without pulling wire for each one. On a retrofit that is the difference between a thermostat swap and opening walls.

The kit version ships with the parts the system needs to be commissioned together rather than sourced separately and hoped to match.

Used with: RedLINK™ accessories.
